THE PROJECT

Overview

Created with GIT 540 Team 9, Journey Through Design offers several ways into art history: explore a timeline, search for a subject, or narrow a collection with filters. The shared Figma project contains a design system, wireframes, developed screens, interactive work, and research notes.

My role: contributing designer and usability testing. The project is a team effort; the screens shown here are shared team outputs. The source includes usability-testing notes credited to Darrell, which ground the observations below.

01 / DESIGN PROCESS

Connect different ways to explore

The timeline provides a broad historical entry point. Filters for time period, nationality, movement, and artist support a more specific search. Artist and artwork pages extend the journey from an overview into a focused subject.

02 / DESIGN PROCESS

Use testing to question navigation

In the mid-fidelity testing notes credited to me, the participant could complete the first task but did not always know how to return. “Going back” was identified as confusing. Filter categories also needed clarification. These observations point toward clearer return paths and more understandable filter choices.

03 / DESIGN PROCESS

Build a consistent visual language

The team’s design system combines Taviraj and Gantari typography with a blue and red palette. Repeated navigation, cards, and controls connect the different page types. Later testing notes credited to me record successful navigation through gallery, search, timeline filters, and artwork; these are qualitative observations from testing, rather than proof of broad usability gains.

REFLECTION

What this work shows

The project connects collaborative interface design with task-based testing. My documented testing contributions show how observations about navigation and filter clarity can inform a team’s next iteration.
